questions.question: Four years ago, Ravi was thrice as old as Kaviraj. At present, Ravi is twice as old as Kaviraj. Find Ravi's age at present.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Ravi** to **Kaviraj** 4 years ago = 3 : 1 (Difference = 2 units)

Ratio of **Ravi** to **Kaviraj** at present = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 unit)

Equate differences by multiplying present ratio by 2 → 4 : 2 (Difference = 2 units)

The change in units from past to present (4 − 3 or 2 − 1) = 1 unit → 4 years

**Ravi**'s present age = 4 units = 4 × 4 = 16 years

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

questions.question: If a sum is invested at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum for 9 months to earn an interest of ₹18,000, what was the principal amount invested?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** for the period = Rate × Time

Effective Rate = 8% × (9/12) years = 6%

According to the question, 6% of **Principal** = ₹18,000

1% of Principal = ₹3,000

100% (**Principal Amount**) = ₹3,000 × 100 = ₹3,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹18,000

**Rate (R)** = 8% per annum

**Time (T)** = 9 months = 9/12 years = 3/4 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70761f051b594e51a3cb0b434a8d918ebef1d51245e3f94a93e2d47c5de4ea25.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 18,000 = (P × 8 × 3/4) / 100

⇒ 18,000 = (P × 2 × 3) / 100

⇒ 18,000 = (P × 6) / 100

⇒ 18,000 × 100 = 6P

⇒ P = 18,00,000 ÷ 6

⇒ P = ₹3,00,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,00,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Components

The formula SI = (P × R × T) / 100 connects four variables; knowing any three allows you to find the fourth. Principal (P) is the **original sum** invested or borrowed.

Time Conversion Rule

For interest calculations, the time 'T' must match the rate's period. If the rate is **per annum**, convert months to years by dividing by 12 or days by 365.

Total Amount

The **Total Amount** (A) is the sum of the Principal and the interest earned: A = P + SI, or A = P[1 + (RT/100)].

questions.question: A regular polygon has 45 sides; each of length 2 cm. The area (in cm²) of the polygon is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The standard formula for the area of a **regular polygon** with **n** sides, each of length **a** is given by:

Area = (n × a²) ÷ (4 × tan(180° ÷ n)) = (n × a²) × cot(180° ÷ n) ÷ 4

Given, **n = 45** and **a = 2 cm**:

⇒ Area = (45 × 2²) ÷ (4 × tan(180° ÷ 45))

⇒ Area = (45 × 4) ÷ (4 × tan(4°)) = 45 ÷ tan(4°) = 45 cot(4°)

Since 45 cot(4°) matches standard area formulas, we simplify to get the required expression from the standard options.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 cot(4°).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of sides (n) = **45**

Length of each side (a) = **2 cm**

**Formula Used:**

Area of a regular polygon of n sides is:

Area = (n × a²) ÷ (4 × tan(π ÷ n))

Where π radians = 180°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (45 × 2²) ÷ (4 × tan(180° ÷ 45))

⇒ Area = (45 × 4) ÷ (4 × tan(4°))

⇒ Area = 45 ÷ tan(4°)

Using the trigonometric identity cot(θ) = 1 ÷ tan(θ):

⇒ Area = 45 cot(4°) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 45 cot(4°).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Regular Polygon with Inradius

The area of a regular polygon can also be expressed as Area = (1 ÷ 2) × Perimeter × Inradius (apothem), where apothem r = a ÷ (2 × tan(180°/n)).

Interior and Exterior Angles

For any regular polygon with n sides, each exterior angle is 360° ÷ n, and each interior angle is 180° − (360° ÷ n).

questions.question: The ratio of land to water for Earth as a whole is 1:3, and it is 2:5 in the Northern hemisphere. If the areas of the Northern and the Southern hemispheres are equal, then the ratio of land to water in the Southern hemisphere is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume total **Earth area** = 28 units (LCM of Whole Earth ratio sum 4 and Hemisphere ratio sum 7 × 2).

Then **Northern Hemisphere (NH)** = 14 units and **Southern Hemisphere (SH)** = 14 units.

**Total Land** = 1/4 × 28 = 7 units | **Total Water** = 3/4 × 28 = 21 units.

**Land in NH** = 2/7 × 14 = 4 units | **Water in NH** = 5/7 × 14 = 10 units.

**Land in SH** = 7 − 4 = 3 units | **Water in SH** = 21 − 10 = 11 units.

**SH Ratio** (Land:Water) = 3:11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3:11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Land** to **Water** (Earth) = 1 : 3

Ratio of **Land** to **Water** (Northern Hemisphere) = 2 : 5

**Northern Hemisphere Area** = **Southern Hemisphere Area**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02b1ce70e6cf04d0cd102ec75f26fb8130c188a12c9405cf9cf94df0ecba6532.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total area of the **Earth** be 280 units (to avoid decimals).

⇒ Total **Land** on Earth = (1 / (1+3)) × 280 = 1/4 × 280 = 70 units.

⇒ Total **Water** on Earth = (3 / (1+3)) × 280 = 3/4 × 280 = 210 units.

⇒ Area of **Northern Hemisphere** = 280 ÷ 2 = 140 units.

⇒ **Land** in Northern Hemisphere = (2 / (2+5)) × 140 = 2/7 × 140 = 40 units.

⇒ **Water** in Northern Hemisphere = (5 / (2+5)) × 140 = 5/7 × 140 = 100 units.

⇒ **Land** in Southern Hemisphere = Total Land − NH Land = 70 − 40 = 30 units.

⇒ **Water** in Southern Hemisphere = Total Water − NH Water = 210 − 100 = 110 units.

⇒ Required **Ratio** = 30 : 110 = 3 : 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 3:11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion Basics

If a quantity is divided in the ratio a:b, the parts are [a/(a+b)] × Total and [b/(a+b)] × Total.

Combining Ratios

When components of a whole are given in different ratios, always assume a total value that is the least common multiple (LCM) of the sum of ratio parts to simplify calculations.

Hemisphere Area Property

The equator divides a sphere into two equal halves (hemispheres), so Area(NH) = Area(SH) = 1/2 × Area(Total Earth).

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 38%. If the cost price is increased by ₹20 and the selling price is reduced by ₹45, then the profit would be 37.5%. What is the original cost price (in ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **CP : SP** ratio = 100 : 138 = **50 : 69**

Final **CP : SP** ratio = 100 : 137.5 = **8 : 11**

Apply cross-multiplication: |(50 × 11 − 69 × 8)| units = |(11 × 20 − 8 × (−45))|

2 units = 220 + 360 = 580 ⇒ 1 unit = 290

Original **Cost Price** = 50 units = 50 × 290 = 14500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Profit = **38%** | New Profit = **37.5%** | CP Increase = **₹20** | SP Decrease = **₹45**

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Profit%)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32588b5e7941d92c7e62fe94f137f418640a64fd19f6bf11a49b12bd57173350.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original **Cost Price** = x

⇒ Original **Selling Price** = 1.38x

⇒ New **CP** = x + 20 and New **SP** = 1.38x − 45

⇒ According to question: New SP = 1.375 × New CP

⇒ 1.38x − 45 = 1.375 × (x + 20)

⇒ 1.38x − 45 = 1.375x + 27.5

⇒ 1.38x − 1.375x = 27.5 + 45

⇒ 0.005x = 72.5

⇒ x = 72.5 ÷ 0.005 = 14500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit occurs when SP > CP. The fundamental formula is **SP = CP + Profit**, where Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Calculations become faster by converting common percentages: **37.5% = 3/8**, which implies SP/CP = 11/8 for a profit.

Cost Price Change Impact

If both CP and SP change, the new profit percentage is always calculated on the **new Cost Price**.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 20 days, respectively. Both work for 3 days and then A leaves. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(12, 20) = **60 units**.

Efficiency of **A** = 5 units/day; Efficiency of **B** = 3 units/day.

Combined work in **3 days** = (5 + 3) × 3 = **24 units**.

Remaining work = 60 − 24 = **36 units**.

Time taken by **B** = 36 ÷ 3 = **12 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 12 days

Time taken by **B** = 20 days

Work duration for both = 3 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of (**A + B**) = 5 + 3 = 8 units/day

⇒ Work completed by both in **3 days** = 8 × 3 = 24 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = Total Work − Completed Work

⇒ Remaining Work = 60 − 24 = 36 units

⇒ Time taken by **B** to complete **remaining work** = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency

When two people work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies. Total Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is identical to work efficiency where filling pipes have positive efficiency and leakage or outlet pipes have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the **ratio of work done** by each person, which is the same as the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same duration.

questions.question: A customer orders food online worth ₹1,000. The food delivery app offers a flat promotional discount of 20% on the bill. After this discount, if the amount falls between ₹650 to ₹800 (both inclusive), an additional discount of 5% is applied on that bill. If the bill includes a fixed delivery charge of ₹80 on all orders, what is the final amount the customer has to pay?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier for **consecutive discounts** of 20% and 5% = 0.80 × 0.95 = 0.76

Bill amount after both discounts = 1000 × 0.76 = ₹760

Final payable amount = **Discounted bill** + **Delivery charge**

Final amount = 760 + 80 = ₹840

**∴ The correct answer is ₹840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial order value = ₹1000, **Promotional Discount** = 20%, **Conditional Discount** = 5% (if price is ₹650 to ₹800), **Fixed Delivery Charge** = ₹80.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8131b16ae5d8ecd397a1ee23aa965023568a7af26087bcdc747949e6eb4ff158.png] 

⇒ **First Discount** = 20% of 1000 = (20 ÷ 100) × 1000 = ₹200

⇒ **Price after first discount** = 1000 − 200 = ₹800

⇒ The price ₹800 lies in the **inclusive range** of ₹650 to ₹800.

⇒ **Additional Discount** = 5% of 800 = (5 ÷ 100) × 800 = ₹40

⇒ **Net food bill** = 800 − 40 = ₹760

⇒ **Final amount payable** = Net bill + **Delivery charge** = 760 + 80 = ₹840

**∴ The correct answer is ₹840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts x% and y% are applied sequentially, the total effective discount is [x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)]%.

Fixed vs Variable Charges

Fixed charges like **delivery fees** or **service charges** are added to the final discounted price and do not receive discounts themselves.

Base Value for Discounts

A secondary discount is always calculated on the **reduced price** (the balance remaining after the first discount), not the original price.

questions.question: A number is divided into two sections such that one part is 10 more than the other. If their ratio is 6:4, what are the two parts of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of parts = 6 : 4

Difference in ratio units = 6 − 4 = 2 units

Since the actual difference is 10: 2 units = 10 ⇒ 1 unit = 5

First part = 6 × 5 = 30

Second part = 4 × 5 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 30 and 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two parts = **6 : 4**

Difference between parts = **10**

**Formula Used:**

Value of a part = (Ratio part / Difference in ratio units) × Total Difference

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29159891c2eddcac50af3f1b5cd64915dcc6ee70e8f90297c7c8cb92a21d2bf7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two parts be **6x** and **4x**.

⇒ Difference between the sections = 6x − 4x = 10

⇒ 2x = 10

⇒ x = 10 ÷ 2 = 5

⇒ First part = 6 × 5 = **30**

⇒ Second part = 4 × 5 = **20**

**∴ The correct answer is 30 and 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities by division. For two parts a and b, the ratio is a:b. If a common factor x is multiplied, the values become ax and bx.

Unitary Method

The unitary method involves finding the value of one single unit (part) first, and then multiplying that value by the required number of units.

Difference between Ratio Terms

If the ratio is a:b and the difference between values is D, then 1 ratio unit = D ÷ |a − b|.

questions.question: A factory produces three types of widgets: A, B, and C. In one week, 12 units of A (average weight 47 kg each), 8 units of B (average weight 62 kg each), and 15 units of C (average weight 53 kg each) are manufactured. What is the weighted average weight of the widgets produced in that week?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **average weight** is 53 kg.

Deviation of A = (47 − 53) × 12 = −72

Deviation of B = (62 − 53) × 8 = +72

Deviation of C = (53 − 53) × 15 = 0

**Net Deviation** = −72 + 72 + 0 = 0

Average = 53 + (0 ÷ 35) = 53 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 53 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Units of **Type A** = 12 (Avg weight 47 kg)

Units of **Type B** = 8 (Avg weight 62 kg)

Units of **Type C** = 15 (Avg weight 53 kg)

**Formula Used:**

**Weighted Average** = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂ + n₃w₃) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + n₃)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2d0571135208b491c4d40e670d5e544aa15bff7453d0f1bcd24b05b6aa6efc8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Units** = 12 + 8 + 15 = 35

⇒ **Total Weight** of A = 12 × 47 = 564 kg

⇒ **Total Weight** of B = 8 × 62 = 496 kg

⇒ **Total Weight** of C = 15 × 53 = 795 kg

⇒ **Sum of all weights** = 564 + 496 + 795 = 1855 kg

⇒ **Weighted Average** = 1855 ÷ 35

⇒ **Weighted Average** = 53 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 53 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

It accounts for the relative contribution of each data point. Formula: Σ(n × x) ÷ Σn, where n is frequency and x is value.

Assumed Mean Method

Simplifies calculation by using deviations from a chosen middle value: Average = Assumed Mean + (ΣDeviations ÷ Total Frequency).

Combined Mean Formula

For two groups with sizes n₁, n₂ and averages a₁, a₂, the total mean is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: A, B and C are partners in a business. A, whose money has been used for 4 months, claims (1)/(8) of the profit. B, whose money has been used for 6 months, claims (1)/(8) of the profit. C had invested ₹ 1560 for 8 months. How much money did A contribute?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** shares A : B : C = 1/8 : 1/3 : 13/24 = 3 : 8 : 13 (taking LCM 24).

Investment × Time = Profit ⇒ (AIₙv × 4) : (CIₙv × 8) = 3 : 13.

⇒ (AIₙv × 4) ÷ (1560 × 8) = 3 ÷ 13.

⇒ 4 × AIₙv = (3 × 12480) ÷ 13 = 2880.

⇒ AIₙv = 2880 ÷ 4 = 720.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A's time (TA) = 4 months, Profit share (PA) = 1/8

B's time (TB) = 6 months, Profit share (PB) = 1/3

C's time (TC) = 8 months, Investment (IC) = ₹1560

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e92306455ff70dca8967bc667cb86c0958ae5211959001173a3db4e30102271e.png] 

**Calculations:**

Total profit share = 1

⇒ C's profit share = 1 − (1/8 + 1/3)

⇒ C's profit share = 1 − (3 + 8)/24 = 1 − 11/24 = 13/24

The ratio of profits of **A** and **C**:

⇒ PA : PC = 1/8 : 13/24 = 3/24 : 13/24 = 3 : 13

Since **Investment × Time = Profit**:

⇒ (IA × TA) ÷ (IC × TC) = PA ÷ PC

⇒ (IA × 4) ÷ (1560 × 8) = 3 ÷ 13

⇒ 4 × IA ÷ 12480 = 3 ÷ 13

⇒ 4 × IA = (3 × 12480) ÷ 13

⇒ 4 × IA = 3 × 960

⇒ 4 × IA = 2880

⇒ IA = 2880 ÷ 4 = 720

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Rule

In a partnership, the profit is distributed among partners in the ratio of the product of their **capital** and **time period** (Profit = Investment × Time).

Compound Partnership

When partners invest different amounts for different periods of time, it is called a compound partnership. The ratio of their effective capitals determines the profit share.

Investment Calculation

Individual investment can be found using the formula: Investment = Profit ÷ Time. If profit shares and times are known, the investment ratio is (P₁/T₁) : (P₂/T₂).

questions.question: The average of 7 consecutive even numbers is 32. Find the sum of the smallest and largest numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any **Arithmetic Progression** (like **consecutive even numbers**), the **Average** is always the mean of the **Smallest** and **Largest** terms.

Formula: **Average** = (**Smallest** + **Largest**) ÷ 2

⇒ **Sum of Smallest and Largest** = 2 × **Average**

⇒ **Sum** = 2 × 32 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total terms = **7**

⇒ **Average** of the **consecutive even numbers** = 32

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Average** = (Sum of all terms) ÷ (Total number of terms)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bab308404ca745159431cabf4be3652059a38cffd5afd6977b3cb4b8ab8ef4d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For an odd number of terms (7), the **Average** is equal to the **middle term** (4th term).

⇒ 4th term = 32

⇒ 1st term (**Smallest**) = 32 − (3 × 2) = 26

⇒ 7th term (**Largest**) = 32 + (3 × 2) = 38

⇒ **Sum of Smallest and Largest** = 26 + 38 = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Property

In any AP, the average of 'n' terms is always the average of the first term (a) and the last term (l). Formula: Average = (a + l) ÷ 2.

Middle Term Concept

For a series of 'n' consecutive terms where 'n' is an odd number, the average is the exactly the {(n+1)/2}th term.

Consecutive Even/Odd Numbers

The common difference (d) between consecutive even or consecutive odd numbers is always 2.

questions.question: The price of a machine is increased by 20%. Due to a fall in demand, the increased price is then decreased by 25%. Finally, the price is again increased by 10%. The overall percentage change in the price of the machine is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **Net Multiplying Factor** method for successive changes:

Net Factor = 1.20 (for +20%) × 0.75 (for −25%) × 1.10 (for +10%)

Net Factor = (1.2 × 0.75) × 1.1 = 0.9 × 1.1 = 0.99

Overall Change = (0.99 − 1) × 100 = −1%

A negative sign indicates a **percentage decrease** of 1%.

**∴ The correct answer is 1% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Let the initial price of the machine be ₹100.

**Step-by-step price changes:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c542f966c61d33710140cd17266c3e58d62dab9c4b6f3fb1279e21552ef16167.png] 

⇒ Price after **20% increase** = 100 + (20% of 100) = 120

⇒ Price after **25% decrease** = 120 − (25% of 120) = 120 − 30 = 90

⇒ Price after **10% increase** = 90 + (10% of 90) = 90 + 9 = 99

⇒ **Overall percentage change** = [(Final Price − Initial Price) ÷ Initial Price] × 100

⇒ Overall Change = [(99 − 100) ÷ 100] × 100 = −1%

**∴ The correct answer is 1% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by: a + b + (ab ÷ 100).

Multiplying Factor (MF)

For an x% increase, the MF is (1 + x/100). For an x% decrease, the MF is (1 − x/100). Net MF is the product of all individual factors.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

20% = 1/5 | 25% = 1/4 | 10% = 1/10. These can be used to solve using ratio methods (Final/Initial = 6/5 × 3/4 × 11/10 = 99/100).

questions.question: Pipes C and D can fill a tank of 3,000 litres in 6 hours and 4 hours, respectively. Working together, how many hours will they take to fill a 6,000-litre tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by **Pipe C** and **Pipe D** to fill 3,000 L together = (6 × 4) ÷ (6 + 4) = 2.4 hr.

Since the new tank capacity (6,000 L) is exactly **double** the initial capacity (3,000 L), the time taken will also be doubled.

Required time = 2.4 × 2 = 4.8 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Capacity of initial tank = 3,000 L

Time for **Pipe C** = 6 hr | Time for **Pipe D** = 4 hr

Capacity of new tank = 6,000 L

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ed76fea29c11cfe99c96ede6fddb9e2db455aa691056f46c984a106f7e5952c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency (Rate) of **Pipe C** = 3,000 ÷ 6 = 500 L/hr

⇒ Efficiency (Rate) of **Pipe D** = 3,000 ÷ 4 = 750 L/hr

⇒ Combined Efficiency of (C + D) = 500 + 750 = 1,250 L/hr

⇒ Time taken to fill 6,000 L tank = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Required Time = 6,000 ÷ 1,250

⇒ Required Time = 4.8 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time for a constant volume of work. Formula: Work = Efficiency × Time.

Pipes and Cisterns Rule

If an inlet pipe fills in x hours and an outlet pipe empties in y hours, the net work in 1 hour = (1/x) − (1/y).

Direct Proportion in Work

If efficiency remains constant, the time required is directly proportional to the amount of work (tank capacity). If capacity doubles, time doubles.

questions.question: The shadow of a tower increases by 20 m when the sun's altitude changes from 60° to 45°. Find the length (rounded off to one decimal place, in m) of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **tower height** h, when the angle changes from θ₁ to θ₂ and shadow increases by d:

Shortcut formula: h = d ÷ (cot θ₂ − cot θ₁)

Here, d = 20 m, θ₁ = 60°, and θ₂ = 45°

h = 20 ÷ (cot 45° − cot 60°) = 20 ÷ (1 − 1/1.7) = 20 ÷ (0.7/1.7) = 34 ÷ 0.7 ≈ 48.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 48.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let **AB** be the **tower** of height **h**. Let **C** and **D** be the points where the **sun's altitude** is 60° and 45° respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c9f439cf7fe88deb7c4e9cdbb41069ae4b7ca0364db38c6805eaf4b27043546.png] 

**Given:** CD = 20 m, ∠ACB = 60°, ∠ADB = 45°, √3 = 1.7

In right-angled triangle **ABC**:

⇒ tan 60° = AB / BC

⇒ 1.7 = h / BC

⇒ BC = h / 1.7

In right-angled triangle **ABD**:

⇒ tan 45° = AB / BD

⇒ 1 = h / BD

⇒ BD = h

According to the question:

⇒ BD − BC = CD

⇒ h − h / 1.7 = 20

⇒ (1.7h − h) / 1.7 = 20

⇒ 0.7h / 1.7 = 20

⇒ 0.7h = 20 × 1.7

⇒ 0.7h = 34

⇒ h = 34 / 0.7 ≈ 48.5714

⇒ h ≈ 48.6 m

**∴ The correct answer is 48.6 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

Commonly used ratios: tan θ = Perpendicular/Base and cot θ = Base/Perpendicular.

Angle of Elevation

As the object (Sun) moves lower in the sky (altitude decreases), the shadow of a vertical object becomes longer.

General Distance Formula

The distance between two points on the same side of a tower is given by d = h(cot θ₂ − cot θ₁), where θ₁ > θ₂.

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance by train. Had the train moved 14 km/hr faster, it would have taken 35 minutes less. If it moved 10 km/hr slower, it would have taken 30 minutes more. Find the distance covered by the train during the journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **distance** relation: D = [S × (S + a) / a] × t₁ = [S × (S − b) / b] × t₂

⇒ [(S + 14) / 14] × 35 = [(S − 10) / 10] × 30

⇒ 5(S + 14) = 6(S − 10) ⇒ 5S + 70 = 6S − 60 ⇒ S = 130 km/h

⇒ D = [130 × (130 + 14) / 14] × (35 / 60) = 780 km

**∴ The correct answer is 780 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in **speed** (a) = 14 km/hr, Reduction in **time** (t₁) = 35 min = 35/60 hr

Decrease in **speed** (b) = 10 km/hr, Increase in **time** (t₂) = 30 min = 30/60 hr

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** (D) = [S × (S + ΔS) / ΔS] × Δt

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7dcae7825db3eb3963723f9874086931d1d1db899c82c4fb39f0dc5ae58738f1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original **speed** be S km/hr and **distance** be D km.

⇒ According to the first condition: D = [S(S + 14) / 14] × (35 / 60) --- (i)

⇒ According to the second condition: D = [S(S − 10) / 10] × (30 / 60) --- (ii)

⇒ Equating (i) and (ii): [S(S + 14) / 14] × (35 / 60) = [S(S − 10) / 10] × (30 / 60)

⇒ [(S + 14) / 14] × 35 = [(S − 10) / 10] × 30

⇒ [(S + 14) / 2] × 5 = (S − 10) × 3

⇒ 5S + 70 = 6S − 60

⇒ S = 130 km/hr

⇒ Substituting S = 130 in equation (i):

⇒ D = [130 × (130 + 14) / 14] × (35 / 60)

⇒ D = [130 × 144 / 14] × (7 / 12)

⇒ D = (130 / 2) × (144 / 12) = 65 × 12 = 780 km

**∴ The correct answer is 780 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between Speed, Time, and Distance

**Distance** is directly proportional to **speed** when **time** is constant (D = S × T). For a fixed distance, **speed** and **time** are inversely proportional.

Distance Formula with Time Difference

When a person travels at two different speeds S₁ and S₂ and the difference between the **time** taken is Δt, the **distance** D = [S₁ × S₂ / (S₁ − S₂)] × Δt.

Average Speed Formula

If a certain **distance** is covered at x km/hr and the same **distance** is covered at y km/hr, the **Average Speed** for the whole **journey** is 2xy / (x + y) km/hr.

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 20%. If the selling price is reduced by 10%, what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100 units.

Initial **Selling Price (SP)** = 120 units (20% profit).

New SP = 120 − (10% of 120) = 120 − 12 = 108 units.

New Profit % = 108 − 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Profit** = 20%

Reduction in **Selling Price** = 10%

**Formula used:**

**Profit Percentage** = ((SP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d09c779d26fd3c9e1eb4a5730f5a4120b17d5264c818ef5197b74d58b7a11a01.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹100

⇒ Initial **Selling Price (SP₁)** = CP + 20% of CP = 100 + 20 = ₹120

⇒ New **Selling Price (SP₂)** = SP₁ − 10% of SP₁

⇒ SP₂ = 120 − (10 ÷ 100) × 120 = 120 − 12 = ₹108

⇒ New **Profit** = SP₂ − CP = 108 − 100 = ₹8

⇒ New **Profit Percentage** = (8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **Selling Price (SP)** > **Cost Price (CP)**. Profit % is always calculated on CP unless stated otherwise.

Successive Change Effect

When SP is changed, the new profit depends on the **original CP**, which remains constant unless specifically mentioned.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on ₹25,600 at the rate of 12(1)/(2)\% interest per annum for 2 years 3 months, compounded annually.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Interest Rate** to fraction: 12.5% = 1/8. For 3 months (1/4 year), Rate = 1/8 × 1/4 = 1/32.

Principal to Amount Ratio: (8 × 8 × 32) : (9 × 9 × 33) ⇒ 2048 : 2673.

Principal 2048 units = ₹25,600 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹12.5.

Interest units = 2673 − 2048 = 625 units.

**Compound Interest** = 625 × 12.5 = ₹7,812.50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,812.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Principal (P)** = ₹25,600, **Rate (R)** = 12.5% per annum, **Time (T)** = 2 years 3 months.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + (R × t)/100) for fractional years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c9bdc032ac62df06dce7698341278f64424e45d069f94a82e0057995c1ee3e5.png] 

⇒ Convert 3 months to years: 3/12 = 1/4 year.

⇒ Annual rate in fraction: 12.5/100 = 1/8.

⇒ Rate for 3 months: (1/8) × (1/4) = 1/32.

⇒ Amount (A) = 25600 × (1 + 1/8)² × (1 + 1/32)

⇒ A = 25600 × (9/8) × (9/8) × (33/32)

⇒ A = 25600 × (81/64) × (33/32)

⇒ A = (25600 ÷ 2048) × (81 × 33)

⇒ A = 12.5 × 2673 = ₹33,412.50

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = ₹33,412.50 − ₹25,600 = ₹7,812.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,812.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Time Period in CI

When time is in the form T years and m months, calculate for T years normally and apply rate (m/12) × R for the remaining fractional part.

Difference between CI and SI

For a 2-year period, the difference between compound and simple interest is D = P(R/100)².

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for two successive years with rates r₁ and r₂ is r₁ + r₂ + (r₁ × r₂)/100.

questions.question: Find the smallest positive integer that leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 3, a remainder of 3 when divided by 4, and a remainder of 4 when divided by 5.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Observe the **common difference** between the **divisors** and their respective **remainders**:

3 − 2 = 1

4 − 3 = 1

5 − 4 = 1

Smallest Number = LCM(3, 4, 5) − Common Difference

Required Number = 60 − 1 = 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 3, 4, 5

Remainders: 2, 3, 4

**Formula Used:**

When the difference between the divisor (d) and remainder (r) is constant (k = d − r), the smallest number is given by: **LCM(d₁, d₂, d₃, ...) − k**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1075ea5e67bdc8d3da1420d2f4d35af6588b71f2228425fc294a8f066c3be203.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference 1 = 3 − 2 = 1

⇒ Difference 2 = 4 − 3 = 1

⇒ Difference 3 = 5 − 4 = 1

⇒ Constant difference (k) = 1

⇒ LCM of 3, 4, 5:

⇒ 3 = 3¹

⇒ 4 = 2²

⇒ 5 = 5¹

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ = 4 × 3 × 5 = 60

⇒ Smallest number = 60 − 1 = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Concept

If a number leaves the **same remainder** 'r' in each case, the number is LCM(divisors) + r.

Successive Division

In **successive division**, the quotient of the first division becomes the dividend for the second division.

Chinese Remainder Theorem

A general method to find a number satisfying multiple linear congruences when divisors are **coprime**.

questions.question: A trader offers "Buy two, get one free" on a certain pair of trousers. If the marked price of the pair of trousers is ₹ 2700, and the trader still earns a profit of 20%, find the cost price of one pair of trousers for the trader.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 13 and their product is 30. The positive difference between them is:

questions.question: Which of the following tasks is exclusive to the role of System Software and cannot be performed by an Application Software program?

options.text: Allocating a specific block of the CPU's processing time to a newly launched program.
Accepting user input from a keyboard and displaying output on a monitor.
Managing data storage and retrieval on a hard disk drive.
Executing a pre-written script to automate a series of repetitive tasks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allocating a specific block of the CPU's processing time to a newly launched program**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **System Software** acts as the essential layer between computer hardware and **Application Software**, providing the necessary environment for other programs to run.
 
• **CPU Scheduling** is the process of deciding which program or process gets to use the **Central Processing Unit** and for what duration. This task is exclusive to the **Operating System (OS)**, which is a type of system software.
 
• The **OS Kernel** operates in a privileged **Kernel Mode**, allowing it to manage hardware resources directly. It uses complex algorithms such as **Round Robin**, **Priority Scheduling**, or **Multilevel Queue Scheduling** to manage **CPU Cycles**.
 
• Application programs run in a restricted **User Mode**. They cannot allocate **Processor Time** to themselves or other programs because doing so would allow a single application to potentially crash or freeze the entire system.
 
• While application programs can request resources, the actual **Resource Allocation** and **Process Management** are strictly handled by the system software to ensure stability and **Concurrency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System Software Categories**:

 
 
• **Operating Systems**: Examples like **Windows**, **Unix**, and **Android** manage hardware, memory, and task switching.
 
• **Device Drivers**: Specialized software that allows the OS to communicate with specific hardware like printers or graphics cards.
 
• **Utility Software**: Programs designed for system maintenance, such as **Disk Cleanup** or **System Restore**.
 
 
 
• **Application Software Traits**:
 
 
• Applications like **Web Browsers**, **Spreadsheets**, and **Video Players** focus on performing user-specific tasks.
 
• Although applications handle **User Input** and **Output**, they rely on **System Calls** to the OS to interact with the **Keyboard** and **Monitor**.
 
• **Script Automation**: Tools like **Macro Recorders** or **Python scripts** are applications used to automate user-level tasks, not system-level hardware management.

questions.question: Who among the following was the most celebrated Indo-Greek ruler in ancient India?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menander I**, also known as **Milinda** in Indian traditions, was the most illustrious and powerful of the **Indo-Greek rulers** who reigned over the northwestern regions of the Indian subcontinent from approximately **165 BCE to 130 BCE**.
 
• He belonged to the **Euthydemid dynasty** and established his capital at **Sakala** (modern-day **Sialkot** in Punjab, Pakistan), which became a major center of commerce and culture under his rule.
 
• His reign is celebrated for the synthesis of **Greek and Indian cultures**. He is the central figure of the famous Buddhist text **Milinda Panha** (The Questions of Milinda), which records his philosophical dialogue with the Buddhist sage **Nagasena**.
 
• As a result of his discussions with **Nagasena**, Menander converted to **Buddhism**, making him one of the first major foreign rulers in India to adopt the faith and patronize its development.
 
• His kingdom was vast, extending from the **Kabul River Valley** in the west to the **Ravi River** in the east, and his influence reached as far as **Mathura** and **Pataliputra** according to various historical accounts.
 
• Menander issued a wide variety of **silver and copper coins** that featured **bilingual inscriptions** in **Greek** and **Kharosthi**, showcasing the title **Soter** (meaning 'The Savior').

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alexander the Great**:

 
 
• He was the king of **Macedonia** who invaded India in **326 BCE** and defeated **King Porus** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes**.
 
• While he opened the route for future Greek influence, he did not establish the **Indo-Greek kingdom**; he retreated from the **Beas River** before reaching the heart of India.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga**:
 
 
• He founded the **Sunga Dynasty** in **185 BCE** after assassinating **Brihadratha**, the last Mauryan emperor.
 
• He was a staunch follower of **Brahmanism** and is known for performing the **Ashvamedha** (horse sacrifice) to assert his sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Rudradaman I**:
 
 
• He was the most famous ruler of the **Saka (Western Kshatrapa)** dynasty who ruled around **130–150 CE**.
 
• He is renowned for his **Junagadh Rock Inscription**, which is the first long inscription written in **chaste Sanskrit**.

questions.question: The Damodar Valley of the Indian sub-continent is mostly rich in which mineral deposit?

__
 
• The **Damodar Valley**, spanning across the states of **Jharkhand** and **West Bengal**, is the most vital mineral belt in India for **Gondwana coal** deposits.
 
• This region accounts for approximately **80%** of the country’s total coal reserves and is frequently referred to as the **Ruhr of India** due to its high industrial concentration and mineral wealth.
 
• The valley contains major coalfields including **Raniganj**, which is the oldest coalfield in India (opened in **1774**), and **Jharia**, the largest and most significant source of high-grade **metallurgical coking coal**.
 
• Other prominent coalfields in this basin include **Bokaro**, **Giridih**, **North Karanpura**, and **South Karanpura**, which fuel the massive iron and steel plants of the **Chota Nagpur** region.
 
• The **bituminous coal** found here is essential for the production of thermal power and the smelting of iron ore in **blast furnaces**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron**:

 
 
• While found in the vicinity of the Chota Nagpur plateau, the richest iron ore deposits are concentrated in the **Singhbhum** district of Jharkhand and the **Mayurbhanj-Keonjhar** belt of Odisha.
 
• The primary ores extracted are **Hematite** and **Magnetite**, which provide the raw material for industries like **TISCO** and **Bokaro Steel Plant**.
 
 
 
• **Limestone**:
 
 
• It is primarily composed of **calcium carbonate** (CaCO₃) and serves as a fundamental raw material for the **cement industry**.
 
• Major deposits in India are located in **Madhya Pradesh**, **Rajasthan**, and **Andhra Pradesh**, rather than the core Damodar Valley area.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium**:
 
 
• Usually obtained from minerals like **Magnesite** and **Dolomite**.
 
• Significant **Magnesite** reserves are found in **Salem** (Tamil Nadu) and the **Almora** district of Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Which resolution from 1931 significantly inspired India’s Directive Principles promoting social and economic justice aims?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karachi Resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Karachi Resolution** was adopted during the **March 1931** session of the **Indian National Congress** (INC), which was presided over by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
 
• It is historically significant because it was the first instance where the **Congress** defined the **socio-economic** meaning of **Swaraj** (self-rule) for the masses.
 
• The resolution included a specific section on **Fundamental Rights** and a **National Economic Program**, drafted largely by **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• It advocated for the **state ownership** or control of **key industries**, **mineral resources**, and **transportation**, which directly inspired the **Socialistic principles** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**.
 
• Provisions regarding **living wages** for workers, **limited hours of work**, and the **protection of women workers** were outlined, which later found a place in **Articles 39, 41, and 42** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The resolution also emphasized **social justice** through the **abolition of untouchability** and the provision of **free and compulsory primary education**, aligning with the objectives of **Part IV** of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lucknow Resolution (1916)**

 
 
• Commonly known as the **Lucknow Pact**, it was an agreement between the **INC** and the **All India Muslim League**.
 
• It focused on **political representation** and a **joint demand** for **Self-Government** from the British.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Resolution (1929)**
 
 
• Presided over by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, this session is famous for the declaration of **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
 
• It authorized the **Civil Disobedience Movement** but did not detail the specific economic justice framework found in the **1931 Karachi** document.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**
 
 
• Contained in **Part IV** (Articles 36−51), these principles are borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• They serve as **guidelines** for the government to establish a **welfare state** based on **social**, **economic**, and **political justice**.

questions.question: What does Article 13 of the Indian Constitution primarily deal with?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judicial Review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 13** acts as a guardian of the **Fundamental Rights** by providing the constitutional basis for **Judicial Review** in India.
 
• Under **Article 13(1)**, all laws in force in India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (pre-constitutional laws) are declared void to the extent of their inconsistency with **Part III**.
 
• **Article 13(2)** mandates that the **State** shall not make any law (post-constitutional laws) that takes away or abridges the **Fundamental Rights**, and any such law made in contravention shall be void to the extent of the contravention.
 
• This article effectively empowers the judiciary to scrutinize legislative and executive actions, ensuring the **Supremacy of the Constitution** over ordinary laws.
 
• The term **'law'** in this context is defined under **Article 13(3)** to include any ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, custom, or usage having the force of law in the territory of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**:

 
 
• While the term is not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution, the power is derived from **Article 13**, **Article 32** (Supreme Court), and **Article 226** (High Courts).
 
• It was declared a part of the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution in the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
 
 
• **Right to Equality**:
 
 
• This is a specific category of Fundamental Rights covered under **Articles 14 to 18**.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Speech**:
 
 
• Specifically guaranteed under **Article 19(1)(a)** as part of the Right to Freedom.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policy**:
 
 
• Primarily governed by provisions in **Article 15** (non-discrimination) and **Article 16** (equality of opportunity in public employment).

questions.question: Which judicial doctrine allows laws promoting DPSPs to be protected from being struck down for violating certain Fundamental Rights, as long as they are interpreted harmoniously?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doctrine of Harmonious Construction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Doctrine of Harmonious Construction** is a fundamental rule of statutory interpretation used by the **Judiciary** when two or more provisions of the **Constitution** or a statute appear to be contradictory.
 
• The primary objective of this doctrine is to interpret conflicting provisions in a way that gives effect to both, ensuring that no provision is rendered redundant or a dead letter, thus maintaining **constitutional consistency**.</

questions.question: Since hydrogen ions cannot exist alone and exist only after combining with water molecules, they must always be shown as which among the following, represented as H₃O⁺?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydronium ion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **aqueous solutions**, **hydrogen ions** (H⁺) are essentially bare **protons**. Due to their extremely high **charge density** and small size, they cannot exist independently in water.
 
• When an **acid** dissociates in water, the released H⁺ ion immediately associates with a **water molecule** (H₂O) through a **coordinate covalent bond**.
 
• This interaction results in the formation of the **hydronium ion**, which is chemically represented as **H₃O⁺**.
 
• The reaction can be summarized by the equation: **H⁺ + H₂O → H₃O⁺**. This indicates that the **acidic properties** of a solution are technically due to these hydrated protons.
 
• While chemical equations often use **H⁺(aq)** for simplicity, it is understood in **Arrhenius theory** and **Bronsted-Lowry theory** that the species actually present is the **hydronium ion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydroxide ion** (OH−):

 
 
• This is a **diatomic anion** consisting of oxygen and hydrogen.
 
• It is the characteristic ion released by **bases** in water and is responsible for **alkalinity**.
 
 
 
• **Oxide ion** (O²−):
 
 
• This is a **divalent anion** typically found in solid **ionic compounds** like **Magnesium Oxide** (MgO).
 
• In water, oxide ions are unstable and react rapidly to form **hydroxide ions**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen gas** (H₂):
 
 
• This is a **diatomic molecule** and is the simplest stable form of **elemental hydrogen**.
 
• It is often produced as a byproduct when **reactive metals** like **Zinc** or **Magnesium** react with dilute acids.

questions.question: According to the Supreme Court of India directives issued in November 2025, which animals must be removed and permanently relocated from institutional public spaces such as schools, hospitals, and railway stations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stray dogs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India**, while hearing **Suo Moto Writ Petition (Civil) No. 5 of 2025** titled 'In Re: City Hounded by Strays, Kids Pay Price', issued stringent directives to address the escalating **stray dog** menace.
 
• A three-judge bench comprising **Justices Vikram Nath**, **Sandeep Mehta**, and **N.V. Anjaria** ordered that **stray dogs** must be removed and permanently relocated from sensitive institutional premises, including **educational institutions**, **hospitals**, **sports complexes**, **bus stands**, and **railway stations**.
 
• The Court mandated that such animals must be **sterilized**, **vaccinated**, and shifted to **designated shelters** or pounds, explicitly prohibiting their re-release into the same institutional areas to ensure public safety.
 
• The directive emphasized that the **Right to Life** under **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India** includes the right to move freely in public spaces without the fear of **dog-bite** attacks, especially for vulnerable groups like children and the elderly.
 
• The **Supreme Court** also directed that all such public institutions must be **properly fenced** to prevent the further entry of stray animals into their compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Legal and Regulatory Framework:
 
 
• The **Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI)** was tasked with creating a **Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** for the humane management and relocation of dogs in compliance with the **Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960**.
 
• The Court noted that the previous **Animal Birth Control (ABC) Rules, 2023**, were being inadequately implemented, necessitating judicial intervention to balance animal welfare with human safety.
 
• **Chief Secretaries** of all States and Union Territories were directed to file **compliance affidavits** within eight weeks to ensure the ground-level execution of these relocation drives.

questions.question: In a classroom discussion about the measurement of work and energy, students are asked to identify the correct SI unit and dimensional formula for these quantities. Which option best represents units for both work or energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**joule and M L² T−²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work** is defined as the product of the component of the **force** acting on an object and the **displacement** caused by that force in the direction of the force. Mathematically, it is expressed as **Work (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (d) × cos(θ)**.
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **joule** (J). One joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of one **newton** displaces an object by one **meter** in the direction of the force.
 
• **Energy** is the capacity to do work. Because energy is consumed or transferred to perform work, it is measured in the same **SI unit**, which is the **joule**.
 
• The **dimensional formula** for **Force** is **[M L T−²]** and for **Displacement** is **[L]**. Multiplying these gives the dimensions for work or energy as **[M L² T−²]**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal**

 
 
• It is the SI unit of **pressure** or **stress**.
 
• It represents one **newton per square meter** (N/m²).
 
• The dimensional formula for pressure is **[M L−¹ T−²]**.
 
 
 
• **Newton**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of **force**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**.
 
• One newton is the force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at **1 m/s²**.
 
• The dimensional formula is **[M L T−²]**.
 
 
 
• **Watt**
 
 
• It is the SI unit of **power**, representing the rate at which work is done.
 
• One watt is equal to **one joule per second** (1 J/s).
 
• The dimensional formula for power is **[M L² T−³]**.

questions.question: What is the primary criterion for the selection of beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Socio-Economic Caste Census, 2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)** was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** in **April 2016** with the primary goal of providing **Housing for All** in rural areas.
 
• The selection of beneficiaries is conducted using the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011** data rather than the traditional **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** lists to ensure a more objective and transparent identification process.
 
• The targeting process utilizes **deprivation parameters** from the **SECC 2011**, focusing on households that are **houseless** or living in houses with zero, one, or two rooms with **kutcha** walls and roofs.
 
• The system employs a multi-stage verification process where the **Gram Sabha** validates the preliminary list generated from the **SECC** database to identify and remove ineligible households based on predefined **exclusion criteria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The scheme replaced the earlier **Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY)** and increased the minimum unit size from 20 square meters to **25 square meters**.
 
• Financial Assistance Structure:
 
 
• Beneficiaries in **plain areas** receive a unit assistance of **Rs. 1.20 lakh**.
 
• In **hilly states**, **difficult areas**, and **Integrated Action Plan (IAP)** districts, the assistance is increased to **Rs. 1.30 lakh**.
 
 
 
• Convergence and Benefits:
 
 
• The scheme converges with **MGNREGA** to provide beneficiaries with **90 to 95 days** of unskilled labor wages for the construction of their house.
 
• It includes **Rs. 12,000** for toilet construction via the **Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G)**.
 
• Beneficiaries are also linked to other government initiatives such as the **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana** for LPG connections and the **Saubhagya Yojana** for electricity.

questions.question: Which device converts **printed text** into machine-encoded text using pattern recognition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**OCR scanner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **OCR**, which stands for **Optical Character Recognition**, is a specialized technology that converts different types of documents, such as **scanned paper documents**, **PDF files**, or **images captured by a digital camera**, into editable and searchable data.
 
• The process begins by scanning a physical document to create a **raster image** (a collection of light and dark dots). The **OCR software** then analyzes this image to identify **patterns** that correspond to alphanumeric characters.
 
• The **pattern recognition** engine compares the scanned shapes against stored **templates** of various fonts or uses **feature extraction** to identify specific strokes, loops, and intersections that define a character.
 
• Once characters are identified, they are converted into **machine-encoded text**, typically using standard encoding formats like **ASCII** or **Unicode**, allowing the text to be processed by word processors or database applications.
 
• This technology is essential for **digitizing** historical archives, automating **data entry** for invoices, and enabling **assistive technologies** for the visually impaired by converting printed text into **speech**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OMR (Optical Mark Recognition)**:

 
 
• This technology detects the **presence or absence of a mark** in specific, pre-determined locations on a form.
 
• It is widely utilized for grading **standardized multiple-choice examinations** and processing **census surveys**.
 
 
 
• **Barcode Reader**:
 
 
• An input device that uses a **laser beam** or **LED light** to capture and read the **parallel black and white lines** of a barcode.
 
• It translates the **width and spacing** of these bars into a numerical code used for **inventory tracking** and retail transactions.
 
 
 
• **MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition)**:
 
 
• Uses specialized **magnetic ink** and unique fonts (such as **E-13B** or **CMC-7**) that can be read by a magnetic reader even if obscured by stamps or marks.
 
• Primarily used by the **banking industry** for the high-speed processing of **checks** and **deposit slips** to enhance security.

questions.question: Which of the following energy resource is considered exhaustible and polluting in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coal** is a fossil fuel primarily composed of **carbon**, formed from the remains of vegetation buried under high pressure and temperature for millions of years, making it an **exhaustible** or **non-renewable** resource.
 
• In **India**, coal is the most critical energy source, powering approximately **70 percent** of the total electricity generation through numerous **Thermal Power Plants** located across the country.
 
• It is classified as a **polluting** resource because its combustion releases significant amounts of **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)**, which is a leading greenhouse gas, as well as **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂)** and **Nitrogen Oxides (NOₓ)**.
 
• The mining and burning of coal also result in **environmental degradation** through **acid rain**, **deforestation**, and the production of **Fly Ash**, which can contaminate soil and water systems.
 
• India possesses the **fourth largest coal reserves** in the world, with major deposits located in the **Gondwana** coalfields of **Jharkhand**, **Odisha**, and **Chhattisgarh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wind Energy**:

 
 
• Considered an **inexhaustible** and **clean** energy source that uses **turbines** to convert kinetic energy into electricity.
 
• India has a high installed capacity in states like **Tamil Nadu**, **Gujarat**, and **Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy**:
 
 
• A **renewable** resource harnessed using **Photovoltaic (PV) cells**, providing a pollution-free alternative to fossil fuels.
 
• The **National Solar Mission** aims to make India a global leader in solar power.
 
 
 
• **Biogas**:
 
 
• A **renewable** fuel produced from the **anaerobic decomposition** of organic matter such as cattle dung and agricultural waste.
 
• It is widely used in rural India as a **cleaner cooking fuel** compared to traditional firewood or coal.

questions.question: Which climatic phenomenon is responsible for sudden winter rainfall in North-West India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Disturbances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western Disturbances** are extra-tropical cyclones or low-pressure systems that originate over the **Mediterranean Sea** and travel eastward across **West Asia** and **Pakistan** to reach **India**.
 
• In the **Indian subcontinent**, they are responsible for sudden **winter rainfall** in the **North-West** regions, including **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Western Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• These storms are carried into the region by the **Subtropical Westerly Jet Stream**, which flows at high altitudes and shifts southward during the winter months.
 
• While the total amount of precipitation is relatively small compared to the **South-West Monsoon**, it is vital for **Indian agriculture**, especially for the **Rabi crops** (winter crops) like **Wheat**.
 
• Apart from rain in the plains, these disturbances cause heavy **snowfall** in the **Himalayan regions**, which helps maintain the glaciers and feeds the **perennial rivers** throughout the year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Local Winds**:

 
 
• These refer to winds like the **Loo**, which is a hot and dry wind blowing in **Northern India** during the summer (May-June), or **Mango Showers** in **Kerala** and **Karnataka**.
 
• They are localized phenomena and do not cause systematic winter rainfall across the North-West.
 
 
 
• **Jet Streams**:
 
 
• These are narrow bands of **strong winds** in the upper atmosphere. While the **Westerly Jet Stream** acts as a carrier for **Western Disturbances**, the rain-bearing system itself is the disturbance.
 
 
 
• **Easterly Waves**:
 
 
• These are tropical disturbances that move from east to west across the **tropics**.
 
• They are typically associated with the **North-East Monsoon** or **Retreating Monsoon**, primarily affecting the **Coromandel Coast** and **Tamil Nadu**, rather than **North-West India**.

questions.question: In the Santhal Rebellion (1855–57), Santhals mainly directed their anger against:

options.text: Missionaries who distributed free food during the famine
Traditional village headmen and clan chiefs of their own tribe
British officers, zamindars, traders and local moneylenders
Solders of the Bengal army posted in distant cantonments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British officers, zamindars, traders and local moneylenders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhal Rebellion**, also known as the **Santhal Hool**, was a massive tribal uprising that took place between **1855** and **1856** against the exploitative **British colonial system** and its local collaborators.
 
• The rebellion was primarily directed against the **Dikus** (outsiders), a term the Santhals used for **zamindars**, **moneylenders**, and **traders** who had disrupted their traditional way of life.
 
• The introduction of the **Permanent Settlement of 1793** by the **British East India Company** converted Santhal lands into the property of **zamindars**, who then imposed high taxes and rents that the Santhals could not afford.
 
• To pay these high rents, Santhals were forced to take loans from **local moneylenders** (Mahajans) at usurious interest rates, often ranging from **50% to 500%**, leading to widespread **bonded labor** and land alienation.
 
• The **British officers** and the colonial **police force** consistently protected the interests of the **zamindars** and **traders**, leaving the Santhals with no legal recourse against systemic fraud and physical oppression.
 
• Led by the brothers **Sidhu Murmu** and **Kanhu Murmu**, along with **Chand** and **Bhairav**, the Santhals declared an end to British rule and aimed to establish a sovereign **Santhal Raj**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damin-i-koh**:

 
 
• In **1832**, the British demarcated a large area of land in the **Rajmahal Hills** as **Damin-i-koh**, intending for the Santhals to settle there as settled agriculturists.
 
• Over time, this area became the focal point of the revolt as the Santhals felt squeezed between the forest and the encroaching **zamindari system**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Rebellion Reforms**:
 
 
• After the rebellion was suppressed with extreme military force, the British government realized the depth of tribal grievances and passed the **Santhal Pargana Tenancy Act** in **1876**.
 
• This legislation provided some protection to the Santhals by prohibiting the transfer of **tribal land** to non-tribals, attempting to curb the power of the **moneylenders**.
 
• A separate administrative unit called the **Santhal Pargana** district was created, making it a **non-regulated** area where special laws applied to respect tribal customs.

questions.question: Akbar’s revenue minister Todar Mal introduced an efficient revenue system based on crop yields, land surveys, and prices called:

• Visual information is processed in the **occipital lobe** located at the back of the **cerebrum**, which receives signals from the **optic nerves**.
 
 
 
• **Thinking**:
 
 
• Higher-order functions like **reasoning**, **planning**, and **problem-solving** are regulated by the **frontal lobe** of the cerebral cortex.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct electronic configurations of the element phosphorus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**K=2, L=8, M=5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phosphorus** is a vital chemical element with the symbol **P** and an **atomic number of 15**. This means a neutral phosphorus atom contains exactly 15 electrons.
 
• The arrangement of these 15 electrons across different energy levels is determined by the **Bohr-Bury scheme**, which provides the maximum electron capacity for each shell using the formula **2n²**.
 
• The first energy level, known as the **K-shell** (n=1), can hold a maximum of 2 × 1² = **2 electrons**. Phosphorus fills this shell completely with its first two electrons.
 
• The second energy level, the **L-shell** (n=2), has a maximum capacity of 2 × 2² = **8 electrons**. Phosphorus occupies this shell fully with the next eight electrons.
 
• After populating the K and L shells, a total of 10 electrons are used (2 + 8 = 10). The remaining 5 electrons (15 − 10 = 5) are situated in the third energy level, the **M-shell** (n=3).
 
• Therefore, the correct distribution of electrons for phosphorus is designated as **K=2, L=8, M=5**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elemental Characteristics of Phosphorus**:

 
 
• Phosphorus is located in **Group 15** (Pnictogens) and **Period 3** of the **Modern Periodic Table**.
 
• Its **valency** is typically 3 or 5, as it has **5 valence electrons** and seeks to achieve a stable **noble gas configuration**.
 
• It exists in several **allotropic forms**; **White phosphorus** is highly reactive and spontaneous in air, while **Red phosphorus** is more stable and used in safety matches.
 
• Biologically, it is a fundamental component of **DNA**, **RNA**, and **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**, which is the primary energy currency of the cell.
 
• The **atomic mass** of the element is approximately **30.974 u**, and it is classified as a **non-metal**.

questions.question: Which of the following was one of the primary objectives of India's 1991 economic reforms?

__
 
• The **1991 Economic Reforms**, also known as the **New Economic Policy (NEP)**, were launched to pull India out of a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis and high inflation.
 
• The reforms were based on the **LPG model**, which stands for **Liberalization**, **Privatization**, and **Globalization**, introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• A primary objective was **Globalization**, which involved **opening up the economy to global markets** by removing restrictions on international trade and capital movements.
 
• This was achieved through the reduction of **import tariffs**, the abolition of **import licensing** for most categories, and allowing **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in various sectors.
 
• The reforms aimed to shift India from an **inward-looking** trade strategy to an **outward-looking** one, encouraging domestic firms to compete globally and improving the quality of products through **technology transfer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberalization**:

 
 
• This process involved the removal of the **License Raj**, ending the requirement for government permission to start or expand most industrial businesses.
 
• It aimed to deregulate the private sector and provide more **autonomy** to producers.
 
 
 
• **Privatization**:
 
 
• This focused on reducing the dominance of the government in business by **disinvestment** of shares in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**.
 
• It aimed to improve **managerial efficiency** and financial discipline in the industrial sector.
 
 
 
• **Economic Context**:
 
 
• Before **1991**, India followed a model of **Import Substitution**, which relied heavily on **import barriers** and **public sector dominance**.
 
• The **1991 reforms** reversed these trends to integrate India into the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** framework and stabilize the **fiscal deficit**.

• The **Census of India** is a decennial exercise conducted by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• The first population census in India was conducted in **1872** during the administration of **Lord Mayo**, though it was non-synchronous and did not cover the entire territory.
